overall: The registered randomized contrasts are well supported: misinformation lowers sharing by 18.2 points and fact-checks by 13.3, and plausibility shows a similar pattern. The close-tie and high-trust results match the tables but are descriptive contrasts on measured attributes. The report has several wording and count slips: a garbled H8 sentence, an unsupported eligible-profile count, and a claim of no dropped data that conflicts with the model Ns. The Abstract's framing of the source attributes and the subgroup claims is also loose. The most important caveat is that the source attributes are not randomized and many tests were run without correction.

issues.issue: The text says misinformation 'was rated more plausible 18.6 points less often'. This is contradictory, and the table estimate is -0.186, meaning less plausible.
issues.fix: Misinformation was rated 18.6 points less plausible than true/neutral headlines (95% CI [-20.8, -16.4]).
issues.disposition_reason: The H8 sentence is garbled; the estimate itself is correct.

issues.issue: H1 text reports chosen shares of 60.3% / 42.1% / 47.0%. The registered summary gives mean_treated of 0.421 for misinformation and 0.470 for fact-check, which match. The wording 'chosen shares' is fine, but the H1 design note says 3,854 misinformation and 3,972 fact-check profiles were eligible, while the table n(level) is 3,822 and 3,915 (analysed N=11,882). No table supports 3,854 or 3,972.
issues.fix: Report the n values from the H1 table (3,822 misinformation, 3,915 fact-check), or cite the source of the eligible counts.
issues.disposition_reason: The eligible counts do not match the table n values and need correcting or sourcing.

issues.issue: The text says 12,000 profile ratings were analysed and none were dropped. The model tables use N = 11,882 (share) and 11,884 (plausibility).
issues.fix: State that the models use N = 11,882 (sharing) and 11,884 (plausibility) of 12,000 collected.
issues.disposition_reason: The prose needs to report the model Ns of 11,882 and 11,884 instead of claiming 12,000 analysed.

issues.issue: The text says close ties still raised plausibility by 2.7 points, and the table shows 0.027. That matches. The text says the moderate-sharer effect on sharing 'weakened to -1.7 (95% CI [-3.5, 0.0])', and the table shows p = 0.056. The text does not state that the effect is no longer significant.
issues.fix: Add that the weighted moderate-sharer effect on sharing is not significant at 0.05 (p = 0.056).
issues.disposition_reason: The prose needs to state that the weighted estimate is not significant (p=0.056).

issues.issue: The text says Spanish respondents shared 'more from low-trust sharers (+7.9 points)'. The table shows a difference of 0.079, which matches, but based on n=257 Spanish and 571 English profiles, so the comparison is thin.
issues.fix: No number change needed; note the small cell sizes (n = 257 and 571).
issues.disposition_reason: This only needs a note on the small cell sizes (n=257 and 571); no re-estimation is required.

issues.issue: Overstated claim: "Misinformation was rated more plausible 18.6 points less often than true or neutral headlines". H8: -0.186, CI [-0.208, -0.164]. The number and sign are right but the wording contradicts itself.
issues.fix: Misinformation was rated 18.6 points less plausible than true/neutral headlines; fact-checks 12.4 points less plausible.
issues.disposition_reason: claim checked against the tables by the checking agent

issues.issue: Overstated claim: "close ties (+3.0 points, 95% CI [1.0, 5.0]) raised sharing". H2: 0.030, CI [0.010, 0.050], p=0.003. Tie strength is measured, not randomized, so 'raised' implies a causal effect.
issues.fix: Close ties were associated with 3.0 points more sharing (descriptive contrast).
issues.disposition_reason: claim checked against the tables by the checking agent

issues.issue: Overstated claim: "high trust in the sharer (+5.7 points, 95% CI [2.3, 9.1]) raised sharing". H5: Trust: high 0.057, CI [0.023, 0.091], p=0.001. Trust is measured, not randomized.
issues.fix: High trust was associated with 5.7 points more sharing relative to low trust.
issues.disposition_reason: claim checked against the tables by the checking agent

issues.issue: Unsupported claim: "none dropped for missing values on the main outcomes; 12,000 analysed". The model tables use N=11882 (share) and N=11884 (plausibility).
issues.fix: State that the models use 11,882 and 11,884 of 12,000 profile ratings.
issues.disposition_reason: claim checked against the tables by the checking agent
